eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent marine layer depth and persistent onshore flow from the Pacific are the dominant drivers keeping San Francisco’s August 19 high temperature probabilities clustered around 70–73 °F. National Weather Service and AccuWeather model guidance show a 2,000–4,000-foot-deep marine stratus layer that limits daytime heating through enhanced cloud cover and cool advection, consistent with typical late-summer climatology where mean highs hover near 67–70 °F. Small differences among the leading bins hinge on forecast nuances: a marginally shallower or more broken layer could allow brief solar warming toward 72–73 °F, while stronger westerly winds or thicker stratus would cap readings at 70–71 °F. Traders are weighting the latest model runs and marine-layer forecasts, which are updated daily by NWS Bay Area, as the key inputs that could shift the narrow 32 %–26 % edge between the top two outcomes before tomorrow’s observation window closes.

Current observations show mostly cloudy skies and daytime readings near 30–32°C, while ensemble forecasts indicate limited convective cooling potential over the next 48 hours. Traders are monitoring the next official 4-day outlook and any late-model shifts in steering flow or moisture that could push the peak above or below the narrow 32–33°C window before resolution.
